claims.text: Machine-learning approaches using expandable features can improve the accuracy of melting-temperature predictions for high-entropy alloys.
Machine-learning approaches using expandable features can improve the computational efficiency of melting-temperature predictions for high-entropy alloys.
The approach can improve predictions of melting properties other than melting temperature.
The proposed model is trained on a dataset of binary alloys.
A model trained on binary-alloy data can be extended to make predictions for multielement alloys.
The expandable features are ndex, σdex, and δ.
Expandable features enable accurate predictions without including multielement alloys in the training data.
The method transforms raw alloy features into an expandable form.
Transforming raw features into expandable features enables prediction of structural phases in multielement alloys.
Transforming raw features into expandable features enables prediction of high-entropy-alloy properties.
Using expandable features reduces the cost of preparing the training data needed for multielement-alloy phase prediction.
The approach will outperform traditional methods in the accuracy of high-entropy-alloy melting-property predictions.
The approach will outperform traditional methods in computational efficiency for high-entropy-alloy melting-property prediction.
The approach is limited to high-entropy-alloy compositions representable by the expandable features.
Prediction accuracy may depend on the quality and size of the training dataset.
Prediction accuracy may depend on the specific high-entropy-alloy composition.
The hypothesis can be tested by comparing model predictions with experimental melting measurements for a set of high-entropy alloys.
Failure to achieve significantly greater accuracy than traditional methods would falsify the hypothesis.
